user.title: Battery
user.description: Name the battery and choose where its power or current is measured.

data_description.system_type: AC-coupled: charger and/or inverter are measured on the mains (AC) side, optionally refined by DC measurements. Typical for grid-connected home batteries. DC-only: all power or current measurements sit on the battery's DC bus. Typical for embedded devices.

sources_ac.title: Sources and bank A
sources_ac.description: Each side needs at least one sensor, AC or DC. A fresh DC reading replaces the AC reading of its side.

data_description.bank_layout: Two banks in parallel share one bus voltage and one state of charge, their capacities add up. In series, bank A is the upper bank: the stack runs from A+ to B-, and A- is connected to B+.
data_description.charger_power_entity: Power the charger draws from the mains. Optional if a DC charging input is set. The sensor can report W, kW or mW.
data_description.charger_power_invert: Flip the sign of this input. Use the same signed sensor for charging and (inverted) for discharging. Negative values are ignored on each side.
data_description.inverter_power_entity: Power the inverter delivers on the mains side. Optional if a DC discharging input is set. The sensor can report W, kW or mW.
data_description.inverter_power_invert: Flip the sign of this input. Use the same signed sensor for charging and (inverted) for discharging. Negative values are ignored on each side.
data_description.charger_dc_power_entity: Power flowing into the battery on its DC bus. If an AC charger input is set too, a fresh DC reading replaces it. Current sensors (A/mA) are accepted and converted with the pack voltage.
data_description.charger_dc_power_invert: Flip the sign of this input. Use the same signed sensor for charging and (inverted) for discharging. Negative values are ignored on each side.
data_description.inverter_dc_power_entity: Power flowing out of the battery on its DC bus. If an AC inverter input is set too, a fresh DC reading replaces it. Current sensors (A/mA) are accepted and converted with the pack voltage.
data_description.inverter_dc_power_invert: Flip the sign of this input. Use the same signed sensor for charging and (inverted) for discharging. Negative values are ignored on each side.
data_description.bank_a_voltage_entity: Voltage of bank A, from A+ to A-. With a single bank, this is the pack voltage. With two banks in series, it can also be the whole stack (A+ to B-), set in the bank B step.
data_description.bank_a_voltage_scale: Correction factor for the sensor (e.g. a voltage divider). Leave at 1.0 when the sensor reports the real pack voltage. The per-cell conversion happens via the cell count.
data_description.bank_a_capacity_ah: Capacity of the bank in Ah. For cells connected in series, enter the capacity of a single cell, because a series connection raises the voltage and keeps the Ah the same.
data_description.bank_a_cell_count: Number of cells connected in series in this bank. Cells in parallel count as one.
data_description.battery_chemistry: Cell chemistry of the battery. LiFePO4 is the only one supported so far.
data_description.soc_curve: Voltage curve used for the voltage-based SoC estimate.

sources_dc.title: Sources and bank A
sources_dc.description: All measurements sit on the battery's DC bus. A single signed sensor can serve both sides: add it to both and invert one of them.

data_description.bank_layout: Two banks in parallel share one bus voltage and one state of charge, their capacities add up. In series, bank A is the upper bank: the stack runs from A+ to B-, and A- is connected to B+.
data_description.charger_dc_power_entity: Power flowing into the battery on its DC bus. If an AC charger input is set too, a fresh DC reading replaces it. Current sensors (A/mA) are accepted and converted with the pack voltage.
data_description.charger_dc_power_invert: Flip the sign of this input. Use the same signed sensor for charging and (inverted) for discharging. Negative values are ignored on each side.
data_description.inverter_dc_power_entity: Power flowing out of the battery on its DC bus. If an AC inverter input is set too, a fresh DC reading replaces it. Current sensors (A/mA) are accepted and converted with the pack voltage.
data_description.inverter_dc_power_invert: Flip the sign of this input. Use the same signed sensor for charging and (inverted) for discharging. Negative values are ignored on each side.
data_description.bank_a_voltage_entity: Voltage of bank A, from A+ to A-. With a single bank, this is the pack voltage. With two banks in series, it can also be the whole stack (A+ to B-), set in the bank B step.
data_description.bank_a_voltage_scale: Correction factor for the sensor (e.g. a voltage divider). Leave at 1.0 when the sensor reports the real pack voltage. The per-cell conversion happens via the cell count.
data_description.bank_a_capacity_ah: Capacity of the bank in Ah. For cells connected in series, enter the capacity of a single cell, because a series connection raises the voltage and keeps the Ah the same.
data_description.bank_a_cell_count: Number of cells connected in series in this bank. Cells in parallel count as one.
data_description.battery_chemistry: Cell chemistry of the battery. LiFePO4 is the only one supported so far.
data_description.soc_curve: Voltage curve used for the voltage-based SoC estimate.

bank_b.title: Bank B
bank_b.description: The second bank. Banks in parallel only need capacity and cell count, banks in series also need a voltage sensor for bank B.

data_description.bank_b_capacity_ah: Capacity of the bank in Ah. For cells connected in series, enter the capacity of a single cell, because a series connection raises the voltage and keeps the Ah the same. Banks in series must have the same capacity.
data_description.bank_b_cell_count: Number of cells connected in series in this bank. Cells in parallel count as one. Banks in parallel must have the same cell count.
data_description.bank_a_voltage_measures: If the bank A sensor measures the whole stack, bank A is calculated as the stack minus bank B.
data_description.bank_b_voltage_entity: Voltage of bank B alone, from B+ to B- (the middle tap to the minus of the stack).
data_description.bank_b_voltage_scale: Correction factor for the sensor (e.g. a voltage divider). Leave at 1.0 when the sensor reports the real pack voltage. The per-cell conversion happens via the cell count.

data_description.empty_v_per_cell: Resting voltage per cell at which the battery counts as empty and the counter is set to 0 %. Pick a value your inverter or BMS reaches before it cuts off, otherwise the 0 % calibration never happens.
data_description.full_v_per_cell: Resting voltage per cell at which the battery counts as full and the counter is set to 100 %. If your charger stops below this voltage, the calibration tolerance still lets the 100 % calibration happen.
data_description.charger_ac_dc_efficiency: Share of the charger's mains power that reaches the battery, from 0 to 1 (0 to 100 %). Typical chargers are around 0.9 (90 %).
data_description.inverter_dc_ac_efficiency: Share of the power the inverter draws from the battery that comes out on the mains side, from 0 to 1 (0 to 100 %). Typical inverters are around 0.9 (90 %).
data_description.charge_efficiency: Share of the charged energy the battery actually stores, from 0 to 1 (0 to 100 %). LiFePO4 cells usually keep about 0.98 (98 %).
data_description.calibration_tolerance_v_per_cell: How far the empty and full thresholds may give way at low current, in volts per cell. At rest the measured voltage is close to the resting voltage, so a reading just short of the threshold still calibrates. At high current the exact threshold applies. 0 keeps the thresholds fixed.
data_description.calibration_hold_s: How long the voltage has to stay past a threshold before the calibration is applied, in seconds.
data_description.voltage_soc_mismatch_warn_pct: Difference in percentage points between the voltage-based estimate and the counted state of charge above which a warning can turn on. A generous value avoids false alarms, because the voltage says little in the flat middle of the LiFePO4 curve.
data_description.voltage_mismatch_hold_s: How long the difference has to stay above the threshold before the warning turns on, in seconds.
data_description.imbalance_warn_v: Voltage difference between bank A and bank B above which the imbalance warning turns on, in volts. Only used for banks in series.
data_description.stale_input_s: Seconds without an update after which an input counts as stale.
data_description.dc_max_age_s: How long a DC reading stays valid, in seconds. After that, the AC reading of the same side takes over again.
data_description.require_fresh_inputs: When on, counting pauses as soon as any input is stale. When off, stale power inputs count as 0 W and voltages keep their last value. The 0 % and 100 % calibration always needs a fresh voltage.
data_description.internal_resistance_mohm_per_cell: Internal resistance per cell in milliohms, used to correct the voltage under load. Leave empty to use the built-in table. The calibration analysis calculates a suggested value from the recorded calibrations, which you can apply from the open setting suggestions.
data_description.full_taper_c_rate: The battery only counts as full when its current at full voltage stays below this C-rate. Leave empty to turn the check off. With solar surplus charging, a small current can also mean little sun, and this check stops the tolerance from calibrating too early. The cell data sheet usually lists this tail current, often around 0.05 C.
data_description.calibration_tolerance_empty_v_per_cell: Tolerance for the empty threshold only. Leave empty to use the shared tolerance, 0 means none. A generous value helps when the BMS or inverter cuts off well above the empty voltage.
data_description.calibration_tolerance_full_v_per_cell: Tolerance for the full threshold only. Leave empty to use the shared tolerance, 0 means none. Keep it small if your charger reaches the full voltage, so a battery that isn't full yet doesn't get set to 100 %.
data_description.calibration_grace_s: How long a short dropout may interrupt the hold time without restarting it, in seconds. 0 restarts it on every dropout. If your charger pauses regularly, set this above the pause length. A stale voltage sensor always restarts the hold time.
data_description.fallback_interval_s: How often the state of charge is recalculated when no sensor reports a change, in seconds.

error.bank_a_voltage_required: A voltage sensor for bank A is required.
error.bank_b_voltage_required: Two banks in series need a voltage sensor for bank B.
error.charge_source_required: Select a charging sensor (AC or DC).
error.discharge_source_required: Select a discharging sensor (AC or DC).
error.current_only_on_dc: Current sensors (A) are only accepted on the DC inputs.
error.ac_source_in_dc_system: A DC-only system cannot use AC sensors.
